title: HSBC Asset Management invests in Model ML’s ‘agentic operating system’ for banks
excerpt: HSBC Asset Management has taken a stake in Model ML, the London startup building an agentic operating system for financial services, through its flagship venture-capital strategy.
content_html:
HSBC Asset Management has taken a stake in Model ML, a London startup building what it calls an agentic operating system for financial services, and the deal says as much about where the industry now thinks the value in enterprise AI is settling as it does about any single company.

The investment was made through HSBC AM’s flagship venture-capital strategy, although neither side put a number on it.

Model ML’s central bet is that the model itself has stopped being the thing that matters. Rather than tie a firm to one provider, its platform routes each task to whichever AI model is best suited to it, so clients can keep pace with advances across the ecosystem without retraining staff or tearing up the way they already work.

It is a pitch that rhymes with other attempts to build the operating system Wall Street never had, and one that quietly assumes the winners will be counted in software rather than model weights.

What that looks like in practice is the automation of the grind. The platform takes on complex workflows across research, due diligence, financial analysis and the production of client-ready documents, while promising to hold on to the governance, accuracy and consistency that compliance officers tend to care about far more than raw cleverness.

The company already works with many of the world’s leading banks, asset managers and advisory firms, and although it launched less than two years ago it has raised more than $100m to date, including a $75m Series A that it billed as one of the largest in fintech history. That kind of pace, in a sector famous for moving slowly, is part of what makes it interesting.

The backer matters here as much as the money. HSBC AM’s flagship venture strategy is a curated fund-of-funds programme run inside the firm’s $81bn alternatives platform, and alongside its commitments to other funds it makes selective co-investments in high-growth, venture-backed companies.

A strategic nudge from inside a global bank is a useful signal for a startup whose entire addressable market is, in effect, banks.

Chaz Englander, Model ML’s chief executive and co-founder, framed the deal as a vote for specialist, vertical AI.

“Rather than a single model, the differentiator is increasingly the software that can orchestrate multiple models across complex financial workflows,” he said, arguing that HSBC AM’s backing reflected growing confidence in AI built specifically for finance. “That’s exactly what we’re building.”

Patrick Sixsmith, who leads venture capital at HSBC Asset Management, was more measured. The investment, he said, reflected a focus on “backing companies operating at the forefront” of the AI and next-generation software that is “driving a new wave of innovation across the economy”.

The timing is no accident, because enterprise attention is shifting from individual models to the systems needed to put them to work.

Money is flowing to whoever builds that plumbing, from startups sending AI agents into the wider enterprise to specialists wiring up agentic banking, and financial services, with both the budgets and the rulebooks, is one of the more attractive places to sell it.

There is a reason a governance-first pitch travels well from London. Banks are among the most heavily regulated buyers on earth, so auditability and consistency are not nice-to-haves but the price of entry, which is precisely the ground a European startup can claim while the larger American labs chase sheer scale. Whether those banks then move quickly is a separate question entirely.

The cheque is undisclosed, model-agnostic routing is a claim plenty of rivals also make, and incumbents from the big consultancies to in-house engineering teams are circling the very same workflows.

The real test is not another marquee name on the cap table but whether Model ML’s agentic operating system survives contact with a compliance department, and turns polished pilots into durable, recurring spend.

content_html_zh:
汇丰资产管理公司 (HSBC Asset Management) 入股了 Model ML，这是一家伦敦初创公司，致力于打造所谓的金融服务代理操作系统，这笔交易充分体现了业界目前对企业人工智能价值的看法，就像它对任何一家公司的看法一样。

这项投资是通过汇丰资产管理公司的旗舰风险投资策略进行的，尽管双方都没有透露具体数字。

机器学习模型的中心赌注是模型本身已经不再是最重要的了。 它的平台不是将一家公司与一个提供商捆绑在一起，而是将每项任务分配给最适合它的人工智能模型，这样客户就可以跟上整个生态系统的进步，而无需重新培训员工或破坏他们现有的工作方式。

这种说法与构建华尔街从未有过的操作系统的其他尝试押韵，并且悄悄地假设获胜者将根据软件而不是模型权重来计算。

实际上，这就是研磨的自动化。 该平台承担研究、尽职调查、财务分析和客户就绪文件制作等复杂的工作流程，同时承诺保持合规官员更关心的治理、准确性和一致性，而不仅仅是原始的聪明才智。

该公司已经与许多世界领先的银行、资产管理公司和咨询公司合作，虽然成立还不到两年，但迄今为止已筹集了超过 1 亿美元，其中包括 7500 万美元的 A 轮融资，该轮融资被其称为金融科技历史上最大的融资之一。 在一个以进展缓慢而闻名的行业中，这种节奏是其有趣的部分原因。

在这里，支持者和金钱一样重要。 汇丰资产管理的旗舰风险投资策略是在该公司 810 亿美元另类投资平台内运行的精心策划的基金中的基金计划，除了对其他基金的承诺外，它还对高增长、风险投资支持的公司进行选择性联合投资。

对于整个潜在市场实际上都是银行的初创公司来说，来自全球银行内部的战略推动是一个有用的信号。

Model ML 的首席执行官兼联合创始人 Chaz Englander 将此次交易视为对专业垂直人工智能的投票。

他表示：“差异化因素不再是单一模型，而是能够在复杂的金融工作流程中协调多个模型的软件。”他认为汇丰资产管理银行的支持反映出人们对专门为金融而构建的人工智能的信心不断增强。 “这正是我们正在建设的。”

汇丰资产管理公司风险投资主管帕特里克·西克斯史密斯(Patrick Sixsmith)则更加谨慎。 他表示，这项投资反映了对人工智能和下一代软件“支持处于最前沿的公司的支持”，这些公司正在“推动整个经济的新一波创新浪潮”。

这个时机并非偶然，因为企业的注意力正在从单个模型转向使它们发挥作用所需的系统。

资金正在流向建造管道的任何人，从将人工智能代理派遣到更广泛的企业的初创公司，到连接代理银行和金融服务的专家，无论是预算还是规则手册，都是更有吸引力的销售场所之一。

治理第一的宣传在伦敦传播得很好是有原因的。 银行是世界上监管最严格的买家之一，因此可审计性和一致性并不是可有可无的，而是进入的价格，而这正是欧洲初创公司在美国较大的实验室追逐绝对规模时可以占据的基础。 这些银行是否会迅速采取行动完全是另一个问题。

这项检查并未公开，许多竞争对手也声称采用与模型无关的路由，从大型咨询公司到内部工程团队的现任者都在遵循完全相同的工作流程。

真正的考验不是股权结构表上的另一个大名鼎鼎的名字，而是 Model ML 的代理操作系统能否经受住与合规部门的接触，并将完美的试点转化为持久的、经常性的支出。
